marrow__ANAT_CH51_Q003.takeaway: From kidney outward, the coverings are fibrous capsule → perinephric fat → renal fascia → paranephric fat.
marrow__ANAT_CH51_Q003.displayText:
From kidney outward, the coverings are fibrous capsule → perinephric fat → renal fascia → paranephric fat.

The 4 coverings of the kidney from within outwards are: true or fibrous capsule, formed by collagen-rich connective tissue; perinephric fat or adipose capsule, which occupies the space between the fibrous capsule and renal fascia; renal fascia; and paranephric fat, which occupies the space between the renal fascia and the anterior layer of the thoracolumbar fascia.
emphasis: From kidney outward, the coverings are fibrous capsule → perinephric fat → renal fascia → paranephric fat

rationales.a: This order places the layers incorrectly; perinephric fat is immediately outside the fibrous capsule, followed by fascia and paranephric fat.
rationales.b: The renal fascia must lie superficial to perinephric fat and deep to paranephric fat, so this sequence misorders it.
rationales.c: This sequence incorrectly starts with perinephric fat; the true fibrous capsule directly covers the kidney.

marrow__ANAT_CH51_Q004.takeaway: Lateroconal fascia extends laterally from the perirenal fascia and joins the parietal peritoneum.
marrow__ANAT_CH51_Q004.displayText:
Lateroconal fascia extends laterally from the perirenal fascia and joins the parietal peritoneum.

The lateroconal fascia attaches the perirenal fascia to the peritoneum. It extends from the lateral margin of perirenal fascia and attaches to the parietal peritoneum. Option A: Gerota's fascia is the perirenal fascia. The kidney and the suprarenal gland are enclosed within anterior and posterior lamina of the perirenal fascia. The anterior lamina of the perirenal fascia blends with the connective tissue surrounding the great vessels behind the duodenum and pancreas. The posterior lamina continues as the lateroconal fascia. Option C: Thoracolumbar fascia is a complex arrangement of multiple fascial layers in the thoracolumbar region. This fascia encloses the paraspinal muscles, quadratus lumborum muscle and the latissimus dorsi muscle. Option D: Treitz's fascia has been used to refer to the fusion fascia behind the head of pancreas.

marrow__ANAT_CH51_Q011.takeaway: Renal papillae project into minor calyces, which join to form major calyces and then the renal pelvis.
marrow__ANAT_CH51_Q011.displayText:
Renal papillae project into minor calyces, which join to form major calyces and then the renal pelvis.

The renal papillae open into the minor calyces. The papilla is the conical apex of a renal pyramid, where the urine from the collecting ducts enters into the minor calyces. The minor calyces unite to form the major calyces, which further unite to form the renal pelvis. The kidney is divided into an outer cortex and an inner medulla. The renal medulla contains many striated and conical pyramids. The base of the pyramid is peripherally located, whereas the apex is directed towards the renal sinus (hilum). The renal cortex is subcapsular and arches over the bases of the pyramids. It extends between the pyramids towards the renal sinus as renal columns. marrow__ANAT_CH51_Q014.takeaway: The left subcostal vein drains toward the hemiazygos system rather than the left renal vein, so renal-vein occlusion does not obstruct it.
marrow__ANAT_CH51_Q014.displayText:
The left subcostal vein drains toward the hemiazygos system rather than the left renal vein, so renal-vein occlusion does not obstruct it.

The left subcostal vein does not drain into the left renal vein. It drains into the hemiazygos vein. So the occlusion of the left renal vein does not impede the blood flow in the left subcostal vein. Veins that commonly drain into the left renal vein (which in turn drains into the IVC) are: + Left inferior phrenic (diaphragmatic) vein, + Left suprarenal (adrenal) vein, + Left gonadal vein On the right side, all the above veins drain into the inferior vena cava directly.

Apart from the veins described above, the first and second left lumbar veins and hemiazygos vein may drain into the left renal vein. Renal veins
